precepts.text: A writing sealed with the king's ring may not be reversed, so a second decree is made to deliver the Jews.
precepts.point: He decreed that the cost be paid from the king's tribute beyond the river so the builders would not be hindered. Once a Persian decree was made it was upheld rather than vetoed. Even in Esther a decree against the Jews was not revoked but answered by a stronger decree in their favor.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

precepts.why:
Darius decreed that Tatnai and his companions be far from the work, that the elders of the Jews build the house of God in his place, and that the expenses be paid “of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the river”, so that “they be not hindered.” Once a Persian decree was made it was upheld, not vetoed.

Esther shows the same law. The king tells Esther and Mordecai to “Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring: for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse.” The decree against the Jews could not be revoked, so a second and stronger decree was written in their favor to deliver them.

That is why Darius did not simply cancel what Tatnai had done. Cyrus had made a decree to build the house, and it stood; Darius confirmed it and made his own decree, and once made, no man could reverse it.

precepts.text: The Most High foretold Israel would be scattered among all people from one end of the earth unto the other.
precepts.point: This is the span of the Persian empire, and Israel was scattered all through it, from India to Ethiopia, not concentrated in one place but spread out during the captivity, which shows we have history in these lands.

note.label: Esther 8: The Decree Reversed for the Jews

precepts.why:
The decree went to “the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.” That is the span of the Persian empire, and the Jews had to be written to in all of it. Israel was scattered all through it, from India to Ethiopia, not concentrated in one place but spread out during the captivity.

The Most High had foretold it: “the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other”. A hundred twenty and seven provinces with Jews in them is that scattering. It also shows we have history in these lands: from India to Ethiopia, Israel was there.

precepts.text: The king gave Esther the house of Haman and Mardocheus his ring, and let them write a decree in the king's name to reverse Haman's letters.
precepts.point: Therefore the first letters sent by Haman are not to be executed, for Haman himself is hanged at the gates of Susa with all his family, the Most High rendering vengeance according to his deserts. The copy of this second letter is to be published everywhere so the Jews may live after their own laws and, on the thirteenth day of Adar, be avenged on those who set upon them.

note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

precepts.why:
The second letter tells the provinces not to execute “the letters sent unto you by Aman the son of Amadatha”, because “he that was the worker of these things, is hanged at the gates of Susa with all his family: God, who ruleth all things, speedily rendering vengeance to him according to his deserts.”

The canonical book shows the king giving the order. “Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand upon the Jews. Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring: for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse.” Haman's letters had been sealed with the king's ring and could not be reversed; so the king gave Esther the house of Haman and Mardocheus the ring, and let them write a decree in his name that answered the first.

That decree is this letter: published in all places, “that the Jews may freely live after their own laws”, and that on the thirteenth day of Adar “they may be avenged on them, who in the time of their affliction shall set upon them.” Vengeance came to Haman according to his deserts, and the reversal to Israel.

precepts.text: In every province where the decree came the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day, and many of the people of the land became Jews.
precepts.point: This is the same lesson for our people today. We are going through days of sorrow, but joy is coming as long as we stay in the commandments and trust in the Lord. Search out the former age and the fathers, for this is the story of our people, and it is history to lean on in our own affliction.

note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

precepts.why:
The king commands the Jews to keep this day “among your solemn feasts” as “an high day with all feasting”. The canonical book records that feasting: “in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day.”

The same provinces where the first decree had brought mourning now had joy and gladness. Almighty God turned the day to joy, and wherever the decree came the Jews kept it as a feast and a good day. “And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.” The fear that had been on Israel fell on the people of the land instead: the “safety to us” of the letter, and the “memorial of destruction” to those that conspired.

precepts.text: The decree went to the rulers of the provinces from India unto Ethiopia; there were Jews living in Ethiopia during the captivity, which is where the man of Ethiopia came from.
precepts.point: People say this proves Philip went to the heathen Ethiopians, but this eunuch was a Jew, part of the remnant of Israel scattered in Ethiopia, in Kush, during the Babylonian and Persian captivity. That is why Christians confuse the Ethiopian eunuch; they do not understand Bible prophecy or Bible history. Candace was a real title of the queens of the kingdom of Kush who ruled from the city of Meroe, and the queen of that time was likely Amanitore, around the same period as the famine in Acts chapter 11.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
In the days of the captivity the king's decree went out “to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces”, written “to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.” There were Jews living in Ethiopia during the captivity, and the decree had to reach them there.

That is where the man of Ethiopia came from. He was a Jew of that remnant scattered in Kush, under Candace, a real title of the queens of the kingdom of Kush who ruled from the city of Meroe. The queen of that time was likely Amanitore, around the same period as the famine in Acts chapter 11.
